title: Dates, availability time and historical features
outcome: Use calendar arithmetic deliberately and reconstruct features using both event and availability time.

exercises.title: Choose a calendar window
exercises.task: Compare one month with thirty days from January 31 in the fixture.
exercises.expected: They end on February 29 and March 1.
exercises.hint: A month is not a fixed day duration.
exercises.answer: The window definition changes which observations belong to a period.

exercises.title: Inspect repeated month addition
exercises.task: Compare two successive month additions with one two-month addition.
exercises.expected: The fixture ends on March 29 versus March 31.
exercises.hint: End-of-month clamping affects the intermediate state.
exercises.answer: Calendar operations should follow the intended business rule rather than an assumed arithmetic identity.

exercises.title: Exclude a future correction
exercises.task: Look up the feature on January 3.
exercises.hint: Filter availability as well as event time.
exercises.answer: A correction about a past event can still be future information.

exercises.title: State cutoff equality
exercises.task: Look up at the exact availability timestamp.
exercises.expected: The inclusive fixture admits the row.
exercises.answer: Real ingestion timing may require another rule, which must be documented and tested.

exercises.title: Preserve entity identity
exercises.hint: Do not choose the latest row from another entity.
exercises.answer: An information boundary also needs the correct relational key.

exercises.title: Handle local civil time
exercises.expected: The standard fixture does not resolve it.
exercises.hint: Dates alone does not supply timezone identity.
exercises.answer: Use a separately prepared timezone-aware policy rather than silently labeling a local clock value as UTC.
